name: trc_inspect_reader
prose: Precondition: invoked via task_call_func() with t the target task and bhp_in pointing to a holdout list head. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL when t is currently running on an online CPU and CONFIG_TASKS_TRACE_RCU_READ_MB is disabled, when t is running and rcu_watching_zero_in_eqs() reports no quiescent state, or when the observed nesting value is negative; otherwise returns 0, and in that case: if nesting is 0 a cmpxchg attempts to change need_qs from 0 to TRC_NEED_QS_CHECKED (which may fail) and the task is not added to the holdout list; if nesting is positive a cmpxchg attempts to change need_qs from 0 to TRC_NEED_QS|TRC_NEED_QS_CHECKED and, only if that cmpxchg succeeds, trc_add_holdout(t, bhp) is called, which adds t to the holdout list, takes a task reference and increments n_trc_holdouts only if t was not already on the list; when t is running on an online CPU with CONFIG_TASKS_TRACE_RCU_READ_MB enabled n_heavy_reader_attempts is incremented and, if rcu_watching_zero_in_eqs succeeds, n_heavy_reader_updates is incremented and nesting is taken as 0, and when t is treated as not running, CONFIG_TASKS_TRACE_RCU_READ_MB is enabled and its CPU is offline, n_heavy_reader_ofl_updates is incremented.
note: Read tasks.h:1667-1712. Reviewer claims: round-1 (return 0 does not guarantee need_qs advanced) RIGHT and in prose; round-2 (trc_add_holdout skips if already listed) RIGHT and in prose; round-15 (n_heavy_reader_ofl_updates only when READ_MB is enabled, in the not-running branch, 1692-1693) RIGHT; prose corrected.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rseq, struct rseq __user *, rseq, u32, rseq_len,
prose: Generated system call entry for rseq(rseq, rseq_len, flags, sig) defined at rseq.c:474-574; the packet name rseq_register_current_task is not defined there. If RSEQ_FLAG_UNREGISTER is in flags it returns -EINVAL for any other flag bit, if current->rseq is not exactly rseq (or is NULL) or rseq_len differs from the registered length, -EPERM if sig differs from the registered signature, or the error from rseq_reset_rseq_cpu_node_id; otherwise it clears current->rseq, rseq_sig and rseq_len and returns 0. Without that flag, any non-zero flags give -EINVAL. If an area is already registered it returns -EINVAL if the pointer or length differs, -EPERM if the signature differs, and -EBUSY otherwise. For a new registration it returns -EINVAL if rseq_len is below ORIG_RSEQ_SIZE or the alignment rules (alignment to ORIG_RSEQ_SIZE for the original size, otherwise the struct alignment and rseq_len >= offsetof(struct rseq, end)) fail, -EFAULT if access_ok fails, if reading the rseq_cs pointer fails, if clearing a non-NULL rseq_cs fails, or (CONFIG_DEBUG_RSEQ) if reading the cpu_id_start, cpu_id, node_id or mm_cid fields fails; on any of these errors the task rseq pointer, length and signature are unchanged. On success it stores rseq, rseq_len and sig in the task, sets notify-resume and returns 0.
note: Packet slice covered only the tail of the syscall; the real function is SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rseq...) at rseq.c:474-574 (macro name per rule 5). Old prose described only the registration path and missed unregistration, the re-registration cases (-EBUSY, -EPERM) and the flags check.

name: sched_fork
prose: Precondition: p is a freshly allocated task_struct for a forked child that is not yet on any runqueue or visible to other CPUs, and clone_flags holds the clone flags of the fork. Postcondition: the function returns 0 on success, or -EAGAIN when, after any reset-on-fork adjustment, p->prio is a SCHED_DEADLINE priority; on every return p->__state is TASK_NEW, p->prio was set from current->normal_prio (possibly then overwritten by the reset-on-fork static_prio), and uclamp_fork has run, and if p->sched_reset_on_fork was set the policy/priority/slice state was reset (for a deadline or RT policy: policy to SCHED_NORMAL, static_prio to nice 0, rt_priority 0 and timer_slack restored; for a negative nice value only static_prio is reset to nice 0; then prio and normal_prio are set to static_prio and load weight and slices are reset) and the flag cleared; on the 0 return scx_pre_fork has run, p->sched_class is set to rt_sched_class when p->prio is an RT priority, otherwise to ext_sched_class when the policy selects SCX (CONFIG_SCHED_CLASS_EXT), otherwise to fair_sched_class, and the entity runnable average, sched_info, on_cpu, preempt count and pushable-task structures are initialized; on the -EAGAIN return scx_pre_fork, the sched_class assignment and all those later initializations have not happened, and no locks or references are held.
note: Read sched/core.c:4695-4764. Reviewer claims: round-1 (class also chosen by SCX policy) RIGHT and in prose; round-2 (scx_pre_fork not run on -EAGAIN) RIGHT, in prose (-EAGAIN returns at 4736-4737 before scx_pre_fork at 4739). The reset-on-fork details are now precise (4715-4733).

name: pick_next_task
prose: Core-scheduling variant of pick_next_task for runqueue rq (sched/core.c:6066-6296), called with rq->lock held; it returns the next task, which is never NULL (WARN_ON_ONCE(!next) is only a warning). If core scheduling is not enabled for rq it returns __pick_next_task(rq, rf). If the CPU is offline it clears rq->core_pick and rq->core_dl_server and returns __pick_next_task(rq, rf). Otherwise it increments rq->core->core_pick_in_flight. If the core core_pick_seq equals core_task_seq, differs from rq->core_sched_seq, and rq->core_pick is set, it takes that previous pick as next (setting core_sched_seq, rq->dl_server from core_dl_server, and clearing core_pick and core_dl_server) and skips to the end. Otherwise it calls prev_balance(rq, rf), saves whether a core cookie was set, resets core_cookie to 0 (accounting and clearing the force-idle counters if there were any, which forces core-wide selection), and increments core_task_seq. If no sync is needed it picks locally with pick_task(rq) and, if that task has no core_cookie, clears core_pick and core_dl_server and goes to the end without core-wide selection. Otherwise it runs pick_task on every SMT sibling, takes the highest-priority pick cookie as the core cookie, replaces mismatching picks by a task found with sched_core_find or by the idle task, counts force-idle siblings, sets core_pick_seq and rq->core_sched_seq, takes rq->core_pick as next, and for each sibling clears its pick if it is this CPU or already running that task, else calls resched_curr on it. At the end it decrements core_pick_in_flight, calls put_prev_set_next_task(rq, rq->donor, next), and, if the core force-idle count is non-zero and next is rq->idle, calls queue_core_balance(rq). prev_balance may drop and retake rq->lock inside balance callbacks; this function does not itself release the lock.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function pick_next_task (CONFIG_SCHED_CORE version) at sched/core.c:6066-6296 read in full. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: early !sched_core_enabled/offline paths skip core-wide bookkeeping (6077-6092); the no-cookie fast path picks locally (6154-6166); old claims that rf is unchanged / lock never released and that BUG() is the failure mode were removed (the BUG belongs to __pick_next_task). I did not verify whether prev_balance drops the lock; wording kept hedged.

name: scx_bpf_create_dsq
prose: Precondition: callable from any sleepable scx callback or BPF_PROG_TYPE_SYSCALL program; if node is not a valid node number (>= nr_node_ids, or < 0 and not NUMA_NO_NODE) or dsq_id has the SCX_DSQ_FLAG_BUILTIN bit (bit 63) set, -EINVAL is returned before any allocation. Postcondition: on success the new DSQ is initialized, inserted into the active scheduler's DSQ hash table, and 0 is returned; on failure the allocated DSQ is freed and nothing is inserted: -ENOMEM when the node allocation fails, -ENODEV when no scheduler is active, -EINVAL for invalid arguments, or the hash-table insertion error (-EEXIST when dsq_id is already registered).
note: Read ext.c:6097-6128: -EINVAL for node >= nr_node_ids or node < 0 and != NUMA_NO_NODE, and for a dsq_id with SCX_DSQ_FLAG_BUILTIN, both before allocation; -ENOMEM if kmalloc_node fails; -ENODEV if scx_root is NULL; otherwise rhashtable_lookup_insert_fast result (0 or e.g. -EEXIST); the dsq is freed with kfree on any non-zero result. Prose correct, kept; old contract dropped (rejected, and the function mutates global scheduler state, rule 4).

name: sched_balance_find_dst_group
prose: Chooses the group of sched domain sd that is best to place task p (woken or forked on this_cpu) among groups intersecting p->cpus_ptr (fair.c:11079-11242); the caller is expected to be in an RCU read-side section (the group list is traversed without taking any lock). It walks sd->groups, skipping groups with no CPU in p->cpus_ptr and those that fail sched_group_cookie_match, computes wakeup stats for each (update_sg_wakeup_stats), notes the local group, and tracks the idlest remote group with update_pick_idlest. It returns NULL if no remote group qualified, and the idlest group if there is no local group. If the local group_type is lower than the idlest one it returns NULL, and if it is higher it returns the idlest group. For equal types: group_overloaded and group_fully_busy return NULL if (SD_NUMA and idlest avg_load + imbalance >= local avg_load), if idlest avg_load >= local avg_load + imbalance, or if 100 * local avg_load <= imbalance_pct * idlest avg_load, else the idlest group; group_imbalanced, group_asym_packing and group_smt_balance return NULL; group_misfit_task returns NULL if the local max_capacity is >= the idlest group, else the idlest group; group_has_spare, with SD_NUMA, may return NULL (this_cpu is on the preferred NUMA node, or adjust_numa_imbalance says stay) or the idlest group (its first CPU is on the preferred node) before the common test, then returns NULL if the local idle_cpus >= the idlest group, else the idlest group. The returned pointer is valid only while the caller keeps the RCU read lock; no lock or reference is taken.
note: Packet name find_idlest_group is the older name; the function is sched_balance_find_dst_group (fair.c:11079). Read in full. Old prose omitted the two early returns (no local group returns idlest; local type greater returns idlest) and described only the NULL cases.

name: sched_balance_rq
prose: Precondition: this_cpu/this_rq are the destination CPU and its runqueue, sd is a valid sched domain whose groups and parent chain are initialized, idle is the balance type, continue_balancing points to writable storage, and the caller holds no rq lock that the function itself takes. Postcondition: returns ld_moved, the number of tasks migrated to env.dst_rq, which is this_rq or, after a destination-pinned retry, the runqueue of the alternate new_dst_cpu (zero when none were moved, balancing was declined, or all were pinned); the busiest runqueue lock is taken and released inside, having released the sched_balance_running serialization token if it acquired it, updated sd's load-balance statistics, nr_balance_failed and balance_interval, possibly set *continue_balancing to 0, possibly set the parent group's imbalance flag, and possibly set busiest->active_balance with push_cpu = this_cpu and queued active_load_balance_cpu_stop work on the busiest CPU.
note: Slice cut the head; real function sched_balance_rq at fair.c:12049-12333 (returns at 12333). Reviewer round-15 claim (returns tasks migrated to env.dst_rq which may be an alternate dst CPU) RIGHT (12177-12178); prose corrected.

name: sched_balance_find_dst_cpu
prose: Precondition: sd is a non-NULL sched_domain, p is a valid task, cpu and prev_cpu are valid CPU numbers, and sd_flag is a valid SD balance flag mask. Postcondition: if sched_domain_span(sd) does not intersect p->cpus_ptr the function returns prev_cpu without calling sync_entity_load_avg; otherwise, when sd_flag does not include SD_BALANCE_FORK it calls sync_entity_load_avg(&p->se), and it returns either the input cpu unchanged or a CPU value produced by sched_balance_find_dst_group_cpu for a group found at some traversed domain whose flags include sd_flag, taking no locks and acquiring no references for the caller.
note: Read fair.c:7654-7705: early return prev_cpu if the domain span does not intersect p->cpus_ptr (7659-7660, before sync_entity_load_avg); sync_entity_load_avg unless SD_BALANCE_FORK; the loop skips domains without sd_flag and groups for which sched_balance_find_dst_group returns NULL or find_dst_group_cpu returns the same cpu, so the input cpu can be returned unchanged. Reviewer claims (return of the input cpu; early return skips sync_entity_load_avg) are RIGHT and already in the prose. Prose kept.

name: check_preempt_wakeup_fair
prose: Decides whether the wakeup of task p on runqueue rq should preempt rq->donor (the fair-class task being run) (fair.c:8978-9110); the caller holds rq->lock. It returns with no effect if the donor entity is p's own entity, if p is throttled, if rq->curr already has TIF_NEED_RESCHED set, or if the WAKEUP_PREEMPTION feature is off. It matches the two entities up the hierarchy (find_matching_se). If the current entity is idle-class and p's entity is not, it takes the short-preemption path straight away (before the policy check and without update_curr): it cancels the slice protection of the current entity and calls resched_curr_lazy(rq). If only one of the two is idle-class otherwise, or if p's policy is not a normal policy, it returns with no effect. Otherwise it calls update_curr on the current cfs_rq; with the PREEMPT_SHORT feature and a shorter slice for p's entity it selects the short action; it then returns if wake_flags has WF_FORK or p's entity is sched_delayed; it may nominate p as the next buddy (NEXT_BUDDY feature, set_preempt_buddy) and, for WF_SYNC, take the action decided by preempt_sync. Then, depending on the action, it either reschedules at once, returns (action NONE), or picks the next entity with pick_next_entity: if the picked entity is p's entity it preempts (cancelling slice protection when the action was SHORT and calling resched_curr_lazy), retries the pick while none was found but entities are queued, and otherwise, with the RUN_TO_PARITY feature, updates the slice protection and returns without rescheduling.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function check_preempt_wakeup_fair at fair.c:8978-9110. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: throttled check is on p (8995); the idle-current path runs before the policy check and without update_curr (9024-9030, 9039-9043); non-normal-policy p returns only after the idle checks; the old prose statement that every path returns without resched was wrong because resched_curr_lazy is called at 9109.

name: can_migrate_task
prose: Decides whether load balancing may migrate task p to env->dst_cpu (fair.c:9661-9766); the caller holds env->src_rq lock (lockdep assertion). It first clears p->sched_task_hot if set. It then returns 0, in order, if p is sched_delayed and env->migration_type is not migrate_load; if the destination hierarchy is throttled for p (lb_throttled_hierarchy); if env->sd->nr_balance_failed is zero and p is ineligible on dst_cpu; if p is a per-CPU kthread; if p is blocked; if dst_cpu is not in p->cpus_ptr (this also increments nr_failed_migrations_affine, sets LBF_SOME_PINNED, and, unless idle is CPU_NEWLY_IDLE or LBF_DST_PINNED or LBF_ACTIVE_LB is already set, sets LBF_DST_PINNED and new_dst_cpu when another CPU in env->dst_grpmask, env->cpus and p->cpus_ptr exists). Once dst_cpu is permitted it clears LBF_ALL_PINNED; it returns 0 (and increments nr_failed_migrations_running) if p is running on the source rq or is its current donor. It then returns 1 if LBF_ACTIVE_LB is set. Otherwise it decides whether p is hot (migrate_degrades_locality result if non-zero, positive meaning hot, else task_hot) and returns 1 if p is not hot or nr_balance_failed > cache_nice_tries (setting p->sched_task_hot = 1 if it was hot), else increments nr_failed_migrations_hot and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head; real function can_migrate_task at fair.c:9661-9766 read in full. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: the old prose said LBF_ALL_PINNED may be set, but the code only clears it (9734); a positive migrate_degrades_locality makes the task hot (9752-9756); the 'returns 1' conditions apply only after the earlier return-0 checks (9678-9740), now listed in order.

name: push_rt_task
prose: Tries to push the highest-priority pushable RT task of runqueue rq to another runqueue (rt.c:1948-2064); the caller holds rq->lock and pull says whether this is the pull path. It returns 0 if rq is not RT-overloaded or there is no pushable task. At retry, if the candidate's prio is higher than rq->donor's it calls resched_curr(rq) and returns 0. If the candidate is migration-disabled: it returns 0 unless pull is true and rq->push_busy is clear, the donor is an RT task and find_lowest_rq finds another CPU; in that case it may get a push task (get_push_task), drop rq->lock, queue push_cpu_stop with stop_one_cpu_nowait, retake rq->lock, and still returns 0 (the reference on the push task is handed to the stopper work). It returns 0 if the candidate is rq->curr (WARN). Otherwise it takes a task reference and calls find_lock_lowest_rq: if no lowest rq is found it re-picks the pushable task; if it is the same task it releases the reference and returns 0; if there is none, returns 0; if it is a different task it drops the old reference and retries with the new task (so a later retry can still migrate and return 1). If a lowest rq was found it migrates the task with move_queued_task_locked, calls resched_curr on the destination, sets the result to 1, unlocks the destination (double_unlock_balance), drops the task reference and returns 1. The result is 1 only when a task was migrated. rq->lock is held on return, although find_lock_lowest_rq may drop and reacquire it internally.
note: Slice cut the head; real function push_rt_task at rt.c:1948-2064. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-1 (returns 1 after a migration), round-2 and round-15 (revalidation failure retries with a newly picked task, which can migrate and return 1, 2032-2052). Old prose said revalidation failure returns 0; corrected. The migration-disabled path always returns 0 even when it queues the stopper work (2011).

name: DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_2(double_raw_spinlock, raw_spinlock_t,
prose: Precondition: lock and lock2 are valid raw_spinlock_t pointers (they must be different locks: double_raw_lock has no equal-pointer check, so equal pointers would self-deadlock). Postcondition: the generated constructor class_double_raw_spinlock_constructor(lock, lock2) acquires both raw spinlocks via double_raw_lock, which orders them by address (lower address locked first, second taken with SINGLE_DEPTH_NESTING), and returns a class_double_raw_spinlock_t guard value holding both pointers; the caller owns both locks and must release them by running the guard destructor, which calls double_raw_unlock on both.
note: Read sched.h:3046-3063: double_raw_lock swaps so the lower address is locked first and takes the second with raw_spin_lock_nested (SINGLE_DEPTH_NESTING); the guard destructor calls double_raw_unlock. Reviewer round-15 claim (equal pointers unsupported, self-deadlock) RIGHT: raw_spin_lock_nested is only a lockdep annotation. Macro-generated, so named by the DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_2 head per rule 5.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(sched_rr_get_interval, pid_t, pid,
prose: Precondition: interval is a writable userspace pointer to a struct __kernel_timespec. Postcondition: no locks or references are held when it returns; it returns -EINVAL if pid is negative, -ESRCH if no process has that pid, the negative errno returned by security_task_getscheduler() if that hook rejects the query, the negative errno from put_timespec64() (typically -EFAULT) if storing the timespec to interval fails, in which case interval may have been partially written, and otherwise 0 with the process's round-robin time slice (0 meaning infinity) stored in interval.
note: Read syscalls.c:1538-1587: sched_rr_get_interval returns -EINVAL for pid < 0, -ESRCH, the security_task_getscheduler error, else 0 with the jiffies slice converted; the syscall then stores with put_timespec64 (error, possibly partial write, returned). Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(sched_rr_get_interval_time32, pid_t, pid,
prose: Precondition: interval is a writable userspace pointer to a struct old_timespec32. Postcondition: no locks or references are held when it returns; it returns -EINVAL if pid is negative, -ESRCH if no process has that pid, the negative errno returned by security_task_getscheduler() if that hook rejects the query, the negative errno from put_old_timespec32() (typically -EFAULT) if storing the timespec to interval fails, in which case interval may have been partially written, and otherwise 0 with the process's round-robin time slice (0 meaning infinity) stored in interval.
note: Read syscalls.c:1589-1600 (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME): same as the native version with put_old_timespec32. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sched_setscheduler, pid_t, pid, int, policy, struct sched_param __user *, param)
prose: Generated function __sys_sched_setscheduler(pid, policy, param), the sched_setscheduler syscall: it is entered from the syscall table with a pid, a policy and a user pointer to a struct sched_param. It returns -EINVAL if policy is negative; otherwise it returns do_sched_setscheduler's result, namely -EINVAL if param is NULL or pid is negative, -EFAULT if the struct sched_param cannot be copied from user space, -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists, and otherwise 0 on success or a negative error code from sched_setscheduler (which may change the task's policy and priority).
note: Read syscalls.c:880-895 and 962-968: -EINVAL for policy < 0; do_sched_setscheduler returns -EINVAL for NULL param or pid < 0, -EFAULT, -ESRCH, else sched_setscheduler result. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(sched_setparam, pid_t, pid, struct sched_param __user *, param)
prose: Generated function __sys_sched_setparam(pid, param), the sched_setparam syscall: it is entered from the syscall table with a pid and a user pointer to a struct sched_param. It returns do_sched_setscheduler's result with the policy fixed to SETPARAM_POLICY (keep the task's current policy): -EINVAL if param is NULL or pid is negative, -EFAULT if the struct sched_param cannot be copied from user space, -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists, and otherwise 0 on success or a negative error code from sched_setscheduler (which may change the task's RT priority).
note: Read syscalls.c:977-980: calls do_sched_setscheduler with SETPARAM_POLICY. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sched_setattr, pid_t, pid, struct sched_attr __user *, uattr,
prose: Generated function __sys_sched_setattr(pid, uattr, flags), the sched_setattr syscall: it is entered from the syscall table with a pid, a user pointer to a struct sched_attr and a flags word. It returns -EINVAL if uattr is NULL, pid is negative or flags is nonzero; otherwise it returns sched_copy_attr's error (-EFAULT if the size or structure cannot be read from user space, -E2BIG if the user size is out of range or too large, -EINVAL if UTIL_CLAMP flags are set with a pre-VER1 size), then -EINVAL if the copied sched_policy is negative, then -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists; otherwise it returns sched_setattr's result, 0 on success or a negative error code, after mapping SCHED_FLAG_KEEP_POLICY to SETPARAM_POLICY and filling the parameters from the task when SCHED_FLAG_KEEP_PARAMS is set.
note: Read syscalls.c:900-939 (sched_copy_attr) and 988-1014: the order of checks and returns matches the prose (-EINVAL for NULL uattr, pid < 0 or flags; sched_copy_attr errors incl. -E2BIG with the size written back; -EINVAL for a negative policy; -ESRCH; KEEP_POLICY and KEEP_PARAMS handling; sched_setattr result). Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigprocmask, int, how, compat_sigset_t __user *, nset,
prose: Precondition: nset and oset, when non-NULL, are valid user pointers to a compat_sigset_t, and the caller's blocked mask is readable. Postcondition: the entry-time blocked mask is saved first; the function returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize != sizeof(sigset_t); if nset is non-NULL it converts the user set (returning -EFAULT if that copy fails), clears SIGKILL and SIGSTOP from it, and applies it via sigprocmask(how, ...), returning sigprocmask's error (-EINVAL for an invalid how) without touching oset; when nset is NULL the blocked mask is left unchanged and how is never validated; finally it returns 0 if oset is NULL, otherwise the result of put_compat_sigset(oset, &old_set, sizeof(*oset)) (0 on success, -EFAULT if the user write fails), which writes the blocked mask as it was on entry.
note: Read signal.c:3431-3452: old_set saved at declaration, -EINVAL on sigsetsize mismatch, -EFAULT on get_compat_sigset failure, sigsetsize unchanged elsewhere, sigprocmask error returned before oset is written, oset gets put_compat_sigset. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE2(rt_sigpending, compat_sigset_t __user *, uset,
prose: Precondition: uset is a writable user buffer of at least sigsetsize bytes when sigsetsize <= sizeof(compat_sigset_t). Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize > sizeof(compat_sigset_t); otherwise it computes the set of pending signals (the union of the thread's pending and the shared pending signals taken under current->sighand->siglock, then intersected with the current blocked mask outside the lock) and returns the result of put_compat_sigset(uset, &set, sigsetsize), which is 0 on success with the converted set written to uset, or -EFAULT if that user write fails.
note: Read signal.c:3455-3499: do_sigpending ORs pending and shared pending under siglock then ANDs with the blocked mask outside the lock; compat syscall returns -EINVAL for sigsetsize > sizeof(*uset) else put_compat_sigset's result. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigtimedwait, const sigset_t __user *, uthese,
prose: Precondition: uthese points to a readable sigset_t in user memory, uinfo is NULL or points to writable user memory for a siginfo_t, and uts is NULL or points to readable user memory holding a struct __kernel_timespec. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize differs from sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT if copying the sigset from uthese fails or reading the timespec from uts fails, and otherwise returns do_sigtimedwait's result: a positive signal number when a signal from the requested set was dequeued (with its siginfo copied to uinfo when uinfo is non-NULL, and if that copy fails the return value becomes -EFAULT even though the signal was consumed), -EINVAL if the supplied timespec is invalid, -EINTR if the wait was interrupted, or -EAGAIN if no signal was pending and the timeout expired or was zero; it returns holding no locks or references.
note: Read signal.c:3827-3915: checks and returns match; do_sigtimedwait returns -EINVAL for an invalid timespec, the signal number, -EINTR if schedule_hrtimeout_range reports interruption, else -EAGAIN. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigtimedwait_time32, const sigset_t __user *, uthese,
prose: Precondition: uthese points to a readable sigset_t in user memory, uinfo is NULL or points to writable user memory for a siginfo_t, and uts is NULL or points to readable user memory holding a struct old_timespec32. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize differs from sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT if copying the sigset from uthese fails or reading the 32-bit timespec from uts fails, and otherwise returns do_sigtimedwait's result: a positive signal number when a signal from the requested set was dequeued (with its siginfo copied to uinfo when uinfo is non-NULL, and if that copy fails the return value becomes -EFAULT even though the signal was consumed), -EINVAL if the supplied timespec is invalid, -EINTR if the wait was interrupted, or -EAGAIN if no signal was pending and the timeout expired or was zero; it returns holding no locks or references.
note: Read signal.c:3919-3948 (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME): same with get_old_timespec32. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigtimedwait_time64, compat_sigset_t __user *, uthese,
prose: Precondition: uthese points to readable compat user memory holding a compat_sigset_t, uinfo is NULL or points to writable compat user memory for a struct compat_siginfo, and uts is NULL or points to readable user memory holding a struct __kernel_timespec. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize differs from sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT if get_compat_sigset fails, if reading the timespec from uts fails, or if a signal was dequeued and uinfo is non-NULL but copy_siginfo_to_user32 fails (the dequeued signal is then consumed and -EFAULT is returned), and otherwise returns do_sigtimedwait's result: a positive signal number when a signal from the requested set was dequeued (with its siginfo copied to uinfo in compat form when uinfo is non-NULL), -EINVAL if the supplied timespec is invalid, -EINTR if the wait was interrupted, or -EAGAIN if no signal was pending and the timeout expired or was zero; it returns holding no locks or references.
note: Read signal.c:3952-3980: -EINVAL for sigsetsize, -EFAULT for get_compat_sigset / get_timespec64 failure, copy_siginfo_to_user32 failure converts a positive result to -EFAULT. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigtimedwait_time32, compat_sigset_t __user *, uthese,
prose: Precondition: uthese points to readable compat user memory holding a compat_sigset_t, uinfo is NULL or points to writable compat user memory for a struct compat_siginfo, and uts is NULL or points to readable user memory holding a struct old_timespec32. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize differs from sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT if get_compat_sigset fails, if reading the 32-bit timespec from uts fails, or if a signal was dequeued and uinfo is non-NULL but copy_siginfo_to_user32 fails (the dequeued signal is then consumed and -EFAULT is returned), and otherwise returns do_sigtimedwait's result: a positive signal number when a signal from the requested set was dequeued (with its siginfo copied to uinfo in compat form when uinfo is non-NULL), -EINVAL if the supplied timespec is invalid, -EINTR if the wait was interrupted, or -EAGAIN if no signal was pending and the timeout expired or was zero; it returns holding no locks or references.
note: Read signal.c:3983-4011 (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME): same as time64 with get_old_timespec32. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(kill, pid_t, pid, int, sig)
prose: Precondition: pid and sig are the raw syscall arguments (pid selects a single process, the caller's process group, or a set of processes/process groups, and sig may be any int, which the callee validates). Postcondition: it returns 0 if the signal was queued or delivered to the target selected by pid, or a negative errno (such as -ESRCH, -EPERM or -EINVAL) if no target could be signalled, the signal number is invalid, or permission was denied; it returns holding no locks or references.
note: Read signal.c:4015-4038: kill builds a SI_USER siginfo and returns kill_something_info(sig, &info, pid). Prose correct (results are 0 or negative errnos as returned by that function), kept; the old contract only restated result <= 0 and was dropped.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(pidfd_send_signal, int, pidfd, int, sig,
prose: Precondition: info is either NULL or points to readable siginfo_t memory, and pidfd, sig and flags are validated by the function itself. Postcondition: the function returns 0 when the signal was delivered, or a negative errno: -EINVAL if flags has any bit outside PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD|PIDFD_SIGNAL_THREAD_GROUP|PIDFD_SIGNAL_PROCESS_GROUP or more than one of those bits set, -EBADF if pidfd is neither PIDFD_SELF_THREAD nor PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP nor an open file descriptor, the negative error from pidfd_to_pid if the descriptor's file is not a pidfd, -EINVAL if the pidfd's pid is not visible in the caller's pid namespace, the copy error (e.g. -EFAULT) from copy_siginfo_from_user_any when info is non-NULL, -EINVAL when info is non-NULL and sig differs from the copied si_signo, -EPERM when info is non-NULL and (task_pid(current) != pid or the effective type is PIDTYPE_PGID) and the copied si_code is non-negative or SI_TKILL, and otherwise the error from kill_pgrp_info (when the effective type is PIDTYPE_PGID) or kill_pid_info_type; on the PIDFD_SELF_THREAD and PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP paths a pid reference is taken and released with put_pid before returning, while the file-descriptor path takes no pid reference.
note: Read signal.c:4045-4198. Checks and returns match the prose (flag validation, SELF_THREAD / SELF_THREAD_GROUP with a pid reference released by put_pid, fd path with pidfd_to_pid, access_pidfd_pidns -EINVAL, siginfo copy errors, sig vs si_signo -EINVAL, -EPERM test at 4120-4122, kill_pgrp_info or kill_pid_info_type). Reviewer round-1 claim (-EPERM also for self thread group) is covered: for PIDFD_SELF_THREAD_GROUP task_pid(current) != pid holds, so the same test applies. Prose kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(tgkill, pid_t, tgid, pid_t, pid, int, sig)
prose: Precondition: none; the function validates its own arguments. Postcondition: it returns 0 when the signal (or, for sig == 0, a permission and existence probe) was accepted for the task with the given pid whose thread group ID equals tgid, or a negative errno: -EINVAL if pid <= 0 or tgid <= 0, -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists or its thread group ID differs from tgid, -EINVAL for an invalid signal number or -EPERM or another error from check_kill_permission, or another delivery error from do_send_sig_info, except that a -ESRCH caused by a failed lock_task_sighand is reported as 0; it never returns a positive value.
note: Read signal.c:4200-4254: tgid/pid <= 0 gives -EINVAL; do_send_specific finds the task by vpid, requires matching tgid when tgid > 0, calls check_kill_permission and do_send_sig_info, and maps -ESRCH from do_send_sig_info to 0 (4221-4222). Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(tkill, pid_t, pid, int, sig)
prose: Precondition: none; the function validates its own arguments. Postcondition: it returns 0 when the signal (or, for sig == 0, a permission and existence probe) was accepted for the single task with the given pid (the internal tgid 0 matches any thread group), or a negative errno: -EINVAL if pid <= 0, -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists, -EINVAL for an invalid signal number or -EPERM or another error from check_kill_permission, or another delivery error from do_send_sig_info, except that a -ESRCH caused by a failed lock_task_sighand is reported as 0; it never returns a positive value.
note: Read signal.c:4265-4272 and do_send_specific: pid <= 0 gives -EINVAL; tgid 0 means any thread group (tgid <= 0 test at 4208). Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(rt_sigqueueinfo, pid_t, pid, int, sig,
prose: Precondition: uinfo points to readable memory of at least sizeof(siginfo_t) bytes; its si_signo need not equal sig in advance. Postcondition: the function returns 0 if the signal was delivered to the process with the given pid, or a negative errno: -EFAULT if copying from uinfo fails, -EINVAL if the copied si_signo differs from sig, -EPERM if the copied si_code is non-negative or SI_TKILL and pid differs from task_pid_vnr(current), or the error returned by kill_proc_info (e.g. -ESRCH if no such process exists, or a permission error); it never returns a positive value.
note: Read signal.c:4274-4301: __copy_siginfo_from_user returns -EFAULT or -EINVAL (si_signo != sig); do_rt_sigqueueinfo returns -EPERM for non-negative si_code or SI_TKILL when pid differs from task_pid_vnr(current); else kill_proc_info. Reviewer round-1 claim (omits -EINVAL) is covered: the prose lists -EINVAL for a mismatch. Prose kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(rt_sigqueueinfo,
prose: Precondition: uinfo points to readable memory of at least sizeof(struct compat_siginfo) bytes; its si_signo need not equal sig in advance. Postcondition: the function returns 0 if the signal was delivered to the process with the given pid, or a negative errno: -EFAULT if the 32-bit copy from uinfo via __copy_siginfo_from_user32 fails, -EINVAL if the copied si_signo differs from sig, -EPERM if the copied si_code is non-negative or SI_TKILL and pid differs from task_pid_vnr(current), or the error returned by kill_proc_info (e.g. -ESRCH if no such process exists, or a permission error); it never returns a positive value.
note: Read signal.c:4303-4315 (CONFIG_COMPAT): __copy_siginfo_from_user32 then do_rt_sigqueueinfo. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_tgsigqueueinfo, pid_t, tgid, pid_t, pid, int, sig,
prose: Precondition: uinfo points to readable memory of at least sizeof(siginfo_t) bytes; its si_signo need not equal sig in advance. Postcondition: the function returns 0 if the signal (or, for sig == 0, a permission and existence probe) was accepted for the task with the given pid whose thread group ID equals tgid, or a negative errno: -EFAULT if copying from uinfo fails, -EINVAL if the copied si_signo differs from sig or if pid <= 0 or tgid <= 0, -EPERM if the copied si_code is non-negative or SI_TKILL and pid differs from task_pid_vnr(current), -ESRCH if no task with that pid exists or its thread group ID differs from tgid, or another permission or delivery error from check_kill_permission/do_send_sig_info, except that a -ESRCH caused by a failed lock_task_sighand is reported as 0; it never returns a positive value.
note: Read signal.c:4317-4340: copy first (-EFAULT / -EINVAL for a mismatch), then do_rt_tgsigqueueinfo: -EINVAL for pid <= 0 or tgid <= 0, -EPERM test, do_send_specific. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_tgsigqueueinfo,
prose: Generated function __compat_sys_rt_tgsigqueueinfo(tgid, pid, sig, uinfo). Precondition: uinfo points to readable user memory holding a compat_siginfo. Postcondition: returns 0 when the signal was queued to the target thread; the error from __copy_siginfo_from_user32 (-EFAULT if the compat siginfo could not be copied from user memory, -EINVAL if its si_signo differs from sig); otherwise the error from do_rt_tgsigqueueinfo: -EINVAL if tgid or pid is not positive, -EPERM if the siginfo's si_code is non-negative or the caller is not permitted to signal the target, -ESRCH if no matching task exists, or -EINVAL for an invalid signal number (from check_kill_permission); no locks or references are held on return.
note: Reviewer round-15 claim (omits -EINVAL from the copy helper for a sig mismatch and for an invalid sig) is RIGHT; both added. Macro-generated compat wrapper (signal.c:4344-), named by the COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4 head per rule 5.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)
prose: Generated function compat_sys_sigpending(set32). Precondition: set32 is a user-space pointer to a compat_old_sigset_t. Postcondition: do_sigpending fills a local sigset_t and put_user stores its first word to *set32, returning 0 on success or -EFAULT if that store fails; the caller acquires and releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Read signal.c:4640-4647: do_sigpending then put_user(set.sig[0], set32): 0 or -EFAULT. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(rt_sigaction, int, sig,
prose: Generated function compat_sys_rt_sigaction(sig, act, oact, sigsetsize). Precondition: sigsetsize equals sizeof(compat_sigset_t) (otherwise -EINVAL is returned), and act and oact are compat user-space pointers or NULL. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize != sizeof(compat_sigset_t); returns -EFAULT if act is non-NULL and any of its fields (handler, restorer when present, mask, flags) cannot be read; returns the nonzero error code of do_sigaction if that call fails; if do_sigaction succeeds and oact is non-NULL it writes the previous sigaction (handler, mask, flags and, when present, restorer) to *oact and returns 0 or -EFAULT depending on whether those writes succeed; if do_sigaction succeeds and oact is NULL it returns 0; the caller acquires and releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Read signal.c:4736-4778: -EINVAL for sigsetsize != sizeof(compat_sigset_t); -EFAULT if any act field read fails (restorer only under __ARCH_HAS_SA_RESTORER); do_sigaction error returned; oact writes OR together, giving 0 or -EFAULT. Prose correct, kept.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE2(rt_sigsuspend, compat_sigset_t __user *, unewset, compat_size_t, sigsetsize)
prose: Precondition: unewset is a user-space pointer to a compat_sigset_t holding the desired signal mask and sigsetsize is the size of the sigset as the compat caller sees it. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL if sigsetsize is not equal to sizeof(sigset_t), returns -EFAULT if get_compat_sigset fails to convert the compat sigset from unewset into a kernel sigset_t, and otherwise saves the current blocked mask into current->saved_sigmask, installs the new set as the current blocked mask, sleeps in TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE (scheduling repeatedly) until a signal is pending, marks the saved mask for restoration on return to user mode via set_restore_sigmask, and returns -ERESTARTNOHAND (-514); no locks or references are held on return.
note: Read signal.c:4915-4959: the compat variant uses get_compat_sigset (-EFAULT) and sigsetsize != sizeof(sigset_t) (-EINVAL); sigsuspend saves current->blocked, installs the set, sleeps until a signal is pending, calls set_restore_sigmask and returns -ERESTARTNOHAND. The round-1 reviewer claim (describes the compat variant as native) does not apply to the current prose, which already names get_compat_sigset. Prose kept.

name: tasklet_action_common
prose: tl_head must point to a valid tasklet_head, softirq_nr must be a valid softirq number (so 1UL << softirq_nr is defined), and the caller must not hold the per-CPU tasklet callback lock. On return, the tasklets present on tl_head at entry have been detached and processed: for each, if tasklet_trylock(t) succeeded and atomic_read(&t->count) was zero, then tasklet_clear_sched(t) was attempted - if it returned true the tasklet's callback(t) or func(t->data) was invoked with trace_tasklet_entry/exit around it, and if it returned false a WARN_ONCE was emitted and the tasklet was neither run nor requeued - and tasklet_unlock(t) plus tasklet_callback_sync_wait_running() were then called; otherwise (trylock failed or count was nonzero) the tasklet was unlocked only if trylock had succeeded, re-appended at the tail of tl_head with t->next set to NULL, and __raise_softirq_irqoff(softirq_nr) was called for it with local IRQs disabled; tl_head at return holds the requeued tasklets in encounter order, plus any tasklets scheduled onto this CPU list while the loop ran (for example by a running callback), the per-CPU callback lock acquired by tasklet_lock_callback is released by tasklet_unlock_callback, and the function does not save/restore the caller's local IRQ state, enabling local IRQs after its own critical sections.
note: Read softirq.c:903-948 and tasklet_clear_sched (839-849). Reviewer claims: round-1 (SCHED bit not set means neither run nor requeued) and round-2 (queue not drained) are RIGHT and already in the prose; round-15 (tl_head also holds tasklets rescheduled during the loop) RIGHT, as the list was reset at entry (908-911) and local IRQs are enabled while callbacks run; prose corrected.

name: static_call_init
prose: Precondition: called during kernel init with the core static call site section (__start_static_call_sites..__stop_static_call_sites) valid; if static_call_initialized is already 1 the function returns 0 immediately without taking any lock. Postcondition: otherwise it takes the CPU read lock and the static_call lock, runs __static_call_init over the core kernel static call sites, releases both locks in reverse order, and if that initialization failed it prints an error and calls BUG() (it does not return in that case); on success it registers the module notifier if static_call_initialized was not yet set, sets static_call_initialized = 1, and returns 0.
note: Read static_call_inline.c:495-522. Prose matches: early return 0 when static_call_initialized == 1, locks taken (cpus_read_lock then static_call_lock) and released in reverse, BUG() on __static_call_init failure, notifier registration when static_call_initialized was 0 under CONFIG_MODULES, then static_call_initialized = 1 and return 0. Reviewer round-15 claim about the old contract is moot: contract dropped (the function writes global state, rule 4). Name from the packet is correct.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(setpgid, pid_t, pid, pid_t, pgid)
prose: Precondition: none; if pid is 0 it denotes the pid of the caller's thread-group leader, and if pgid is 0 it denotes that same pid. Postcondition: on success it returns 0 and the target thread-group leader's process group is set to pgid (when pgid == pid, to the target's own pid; otherwise to the process group named by pgid, which must belong to a task in the caller's session); otherwise it returns -EINVAL if pgid < 0 or the target is not a thread-group leader, -ESRCH if no task has the given pid or the target is neither the caller's group leader nor a child of the caller's thread group, -EPERM if the target is the caller's child in a different session, if the target is already a session leader, or if pgid != pid and no process group with that id exists or its task is in a different session, -EACCES if the target is the caller's child that has already executed (i.e., not PF_FORKNOEXEC), or the negative value returned by security_task_setpgid; in every failure case the target's process group is unchanged, the tasklist and RCU read locks are released, and any allocated pid references are freed before returning.
note: Read sys.c:1114-1185. Return paths verified: -EINVAL for pgid < 0 (before locks) or a non-leader target; -ESRCH when no task or when the target is neither the caller's group leader nor a child of its thread group; -EPERM for a child in a different session, a session leader target, or (pgid != pid) a missing pgrp or one in another session; -EACCES for a child that has exec'd (no PF_FORKNOEXEC, 1148-1150); security_task_setpgid error; success leaves the pgrp unchanged if already equal. Round-2 reviewer claim (-ESRCH wrongly includes the already-executed child) is RIGHT and not present in the current prose, which says -EACCES. Prose kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(prctl, int, option, unsigned long, arg2, unsigned long,
prose: Generated system call entry for prctl(option, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5), defined at sys.c:2518. It first calls security_task_prctl; if that returns anything other than -ENOSYS the value is returned at once. Otherwise it sets error to 0 and switches on option: each PR_* option is handled inline or by a helper (for example PR_SET_NAME with strncpy_from_user, set_task_comm and -EFAULT on a bad pointer; PR_GET_NAME with copy_to_user; PR_SET/GET_TIMING; PR_GET/SET_TIMERSLACK; PR_MCE_KILL; PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS; PR_SET_SECCOMP; PR_SET_MM; PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER; PR_SET_IO_FLUSHER; PR_SET_MEMORY_MERGE with mmap_write_lock_killable returning -EINTR; PR_GET_AUXV; the architecture-specific options via their macros). Many options validate unused arguments and return -EINVAL, -EPERM or -EFAULT directly. Query options return the queried value (for example PR_GET_TIMING returns PR_TIMING_STATISTICAL, PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS returns 1 or 0); PR_SET_TIMING and PR_SET_TIMERSLACK can return 0 without updating anything. The result is the option handler value (0, a non-negative query result, or a negative errno); a locked mmap lock is released before return.
note: Packet item SyS_prctl is the generated wrapper of SYSCALL_DEFINE5(prctl...) (sys.c:2518); rec 24 lists the same function. Read the option switch (2530-2870) and the security hook (2525-2527). I did not enumerate every option; the summary lists the return-value classes I verified. Old contract (security_task_prctl clause) dropped.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(prctl, int, option, unsigned long, arg2, unsigned long, arg3,
prose: Generated system call entry for prctl(option, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5), defined at sys.c:2518. It first calls security_task_prctl; if that returns anything other than -ENOSYS the value is returned at once. Otherwise it sets error to 0 and switches on option: each PR_* option is handled inline or by a helper (for example PR_SET_NAME with strncpy_from_user, set_task_comm and -EFAULT on a bad pointer; PR_GET_NAME with copy_to_user; PR_SET/GET_TIMING; PR_GET/SET_TIMERSLACK; PR_MCE_KILL; PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS; PR_SET_SECCOMP; PR_SET_MM; PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER; PR_SET_IO_FLUSHER; PR_SET_MEMORY_MERGE with mmap_write_lock_killable returning -EINTR; PR_GET_AUXV; the architecture-specific options via their macros). Many options validate unused arguments and return -EINVAL, -EPERM or -EFAULT directly. Query options return the queried value (for example PR_GET_TIMING returns PR_TIMING_STATISTICAL, PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS returns 1 or 0); PR_SET_TIMING and PR_SET_TIMERSLACK can return 0 without updating anything. The result is the option handler value (0, a non-negative query result, or a negative errno); a locked mmap lock is released before return.
note: Same function as rec 23 (SYSCALL_DEFINE5(prctl...)); the packet called it __do_sys_prctl. Reviewer round-15 claim (PR_SET_TIMING and PR_SET_TIMERSLACK can return 0 without updating state) is RIGHT (2583-2586 for a bad arg2 returns -EINVAL but a valid PR_TIMING_STATISTICAL changes nothing; PR_SET_TIMERSLACK with arg2 handling at 2630-2638), now stated. The old prose claimed 'on success the requested task state has been updated'.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(setpriority, int, which, int, who, int, niceval)
prose: Generated system call entry for setpriority(which, who, niceval) defined at sys.c:259-321. It returns -EINVAL if which is outside PRIO_PROCESS..PRIO_USER. Otherwise it clamps niceval to MIN_NICE..MAX_NICE, starts with error = -ESRCH, and under rcu_read_lock applies set_one_prio to the selected tasks: for PRIO_PROCESS the task named by who (current if who is 0); for PRIO_PGRP every thread of the process group (who, or the current group if 0) under read_lock(tasklist_lock); for PRIO_USER every thread whose uid is the given user (uid 0 meaning the caller's), after find_user for another user, and if there is no such user it stops with -ESRCH; a user reference from find_user is freed. set_one_prio(p, niceval, error) returns -EPERM if the caller's euid matches neither p's uid nor euid and the caller lacks CAP_SYS_NICE in p's user namespace, -EACCES if it would lower p's nice value and can_nice refuses, the error from security_task_setnice, or otherwise, after turning an incoming -ESRCH into 0 and calling set_user_nice, the incoming error unchanged. So an earlier failure is not cleared by a later success; the final value is -ESRCH if no task was matched, otherwise the last failure's error, or 0 if every task was updated. The RCU read lock and tasklist lock are released before returning.
note: Macro-generated syscall wrapper, named by the SYSCALL_DEFINE3 head per rule 5 (packet name setpriority). Read sys.c:219-321. Old prose was WRONG about -EPERM (lowering nice without permission is -EACCES via can_nice, 243-246) and invented a 'task already has the requested nice value and is not in the caller's thread group' case that is not in the code; the incoming-error chaining is now spelled out.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(getpriority, int, which, int, who)
prose: Generated function __se_sys_getpriority; precondition: the caller holds no locks and passes which and who as plain integers. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL if which is outside PRIO_PROCESS..PRIO_USER; otherwise it returns -ESRCH if no matching task, process group or user process was found (a nonzero who naming no task or pid, an empty group, or a PRIO_USER uid that maps to no user or has no processes), and otherwise the maximum over all matching tasks of 20 minus the task's nice value, a value in 1..40; the RCU read-side critical section and the tasklist lock are always released and any user reference taken by find_user is freed before returning.
note: Read sys.c:329-392: -EINVAL for a bad 'which'; retval starts at -ESRCH; each matching task contributes nice_to_rlimit(task_nice(p)) = 20 - nice, taking the maximum; PRIO_USER with no such user leaves -ESRCH; rcu_read_lock/tasklist_lock released and find_user reference freed. Prose correct, kept.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(setregid, gid_t, rgid, gid_t, egid)
prose: Generated function __se_sys_setregid; precondition: the caller holds no locks and passes rgid and egid as gid_t values, each either (gid_t)-1 meaning no change or a gid intended to be valid in the current user namespace. Postcondition: the function returns exactly what __sys_setregid(rgid, egid) returns: 0 on success with the new credentials committed, or -EINVAL if a non-(-1) argument is not a valid gid in the current user namespace, -ENOMEM if credential preparation fails, -EPERM if the caller lacks the required permission, or the negative error from the security_task_fix_setgid LSM hook, with the caller's credentials unchanged on every failure.
note: Read sys.c:469-472: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(setregid) returns __sys_setregid(rgid, egid); the error returns listed in the prose (-EINVAL, -ENOMEM, -EPERM, LSM hook error) correspond to __sys_setregid (sys.c:425-450). Prose correct, kept.
